unextracted: a macro; the extractor records declarations, not macros
why:
`RCLCPP_FATAL_THROTTLE(logger, clock, period, ...)` -- REFUSE-LOUD (issue 1019, RFC-0089 W3.a). It used to expand to the plain `RCLCPP_FATAL` with `clock` and the period left UNEVALUATED, so a 1 Hz throttle logged at loop rate and a side-effecting clock expression was dropped -- compiles-and-differs. The refusal stands on the CLOCK argument (issue 1302 corrected the reason it used to give): upstream measures the window on the `clock` passed in, while C's `NROS_LOG_*_THROTTLE` (phase-417 W4.d) measures it on `nros_log`'s own clock, so forwarding would drop `clock` and compile and differ.

SITE: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp` is the macro; it expands to `rclcpp::detail::throttle_is_refused(logger, clock, period, __VA_ARGS__)` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp`), a variadic function template whose body is `static_assert(refuse<Logger>::value, NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_THROTTLE)`; message `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp`. Variadic so the arguments are still parsed and type-checked -- only the assertion stops the build, with the migration attached. Probe: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_log_throttle_probe.cpp`.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR at the call, naming `NROS_LOG_*_THROTTLE` (un-clocked) and rate-limiting at the call site as the alternatives.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06): recorded on a MACRO key, like `cpp:RCLCPP_FATAL`. The clang extractor emits no macros, so this key appears in no report and no gate can demand it; it exists so the refusal `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_THROTTLE` has a row at all.
